title: Japan Raises Interest Rates to 31-Year High
subtitle: The Bank of Japan acts to control rising prices as global economic uncertainty continues.

summary.en: Japan’s central bank has increased its main interest rate to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995. This decision aims to control inflation, which is rising due to the ongoing conflict in Iran. The move follows similar actions by other major central banks around the world. While the bank’s governor says future changes depend on economic data, investors are watching closely for further updates. The decision has already affected the value of the Japanese yen and local stock markets.
summary.zh: 日本中央銀行已將主要利率調升至百分之一點二五，為一九九五年以來最高水準。此決策旨在控制因伊朗持續衝突而上升的通貨膨脹。此舉跟隨了全球其他主要央行的類似行動。雖然該行總裁表示未來的調整取決於經濟數據，但投資人正密切關注後續更新。此決策已影響日圓匯率及當地股市。

paragraphs.en: Japan’s central bank has taken a major step to manage the country’s economy by raising interest rates to their highest level in 31 years. The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to increase its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%. This is the highest rate seen in the country since 1995. The decision comes as part of a global trend, with central banks in the United States and Europe also tightening monetary policy—a strategy used to control the amount of money in the economy to stop prices from rising too quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 日本中央銀行採取了重大舉措來管理國家經濟，將利率調升至三十一年來的最高水準。日本銀行（Bank of Japan）投票決定將目標利率從百分之一調升至百分之一點二五。這是該國自一九九五年以來見到的最高利率。這項決策是全球趨勢的一部分，美國與歐洲的中央銀行也都在緊縮貨幣政策，這是一種用來控制經濟體中貨幣總量，以阻止物價過快上漲的策略。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, this move is a direct attempt to combat global inflation, which is the general increase in prices for goods and services, linked to the war in Iran. The conflict in the Middle East has created economic pressure worldwide, forcing central banks to adjust their policies. While the Bank of England recently decided to keep its own rates steady at 3.75%, it warned that future increases might be necessary if the situation in Iran continues to affect global markets.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，此舉是為了直接對抗全球通貨膨脹，也就是商品與服務價格的普遍上漲，這與伊朗的戰爭有關。中東地區的衝突在全球造成經濟壓力，迫使各國央行調整政策。雖然英格蘭銀行（Bank of England）近期決定將利率維持在百分之三點七五，但該行警告，若伊朗局勢持續影響全球市場，未來可能仍有必要調升利率。

paragraphs.en: Not everyone at the Bank of Japan agreed with the decision. The policy committee’s vote was not unanimous, meaning not everyone voted the same way. Two of the nine board members disagreed with the increase. This division suggests that there is still debate among officials about how quickly Japan should make borrowing money more expensive. Kazuo Ueda, the governor of the BoJ, explained that the bank is now focused on ensuring that inflation stays near its 2% target. In August, Japan’s inflation rate was 1.9%, showing that prices are getting very close to the bank's goal.
paragraphs.zh: 日本銀行內部並非所有人都同意這項決策。政策委員會的投票並非全體一致，這意味著並非所有人都投下相同的票。九名董事會成員中有兩名反對調升。這種分歧顯示官員們對於日本應以多快的速度提高借貸成本，內部仍存在辯論。日本銀行總裁植田和男（Kazuo Ueda）解釋，該行目前專注於確保通貨膨脹率維持在百分之二的目標附近。八月份，日本的通貨膨脹率為百分之一點九，顯示物價已非常接近該行的目標。

paragraphs.en: Governor Ueda noted that the bank does not have a set plan for when the next rate increase might happen. “That depends on how price conditions develop,” he said. He added that the bank will analyze data carefully and take action as needed. While he did not rule out the possibility of raising rates again soon, he also stated that the bank does not have a fixed schedule, such as raising rates every three months. The committee meets about once every six weeks, and each meeting will be used to decide the best path forward for the Japanese economy.
paragraphs.zh: 植田總裁指出，該行對於下一次升息的時間點並無既定計畫。他表示：「這取決於物價狀況如何發展。」他補充說，該行將仔細分析數據並視需要採取行動。雖然他並未排除近期再次升息的可能性，但也說明該行沒有固定的時間表，例如每三個月升息一次。委員會大約每六週開會一次，每次會議都將用於決定日本經濟的最佳前進方向。

paragraphs.en: This decision is also important because of the recent weakness of the Japanese yen. The yen has been falling in value against the US dollar for much of this year. In late July, the US Treasury even took the unusual step of selling at least $10 billion in euros to buy yen, helping to stop the currency’s slide to a 40-year low. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently warned currency traders not to bet against the yen, suggesting that the US and Japan are working together to keep the currency stable. Following the latest rate hike, the Japanese currency weakened by more than 1% against the dollar, while the Nikkei stock market index rose by nearly 2%.
paragraphs.zh: 這項決策之所以重要，還因為日圓近期的疲軟。今年大部分時間，日圓兌美元的價值一直在下跌。七月下旬，美國財政部甚至採取了罕見的行動，賣出至少一百億美元的歐元來買進日圓，以協助阻止該貨幣跌至四十年來的低點。美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）近期警告貨幣交易員不要放空日圓，暗示美日兩國正合作維持貨幣穩定。在最新一次升息後，日圓兌美元匯率下跌超過百分之一，而日經股票市場指數則上漲近百分之二。

paragraphs.en: Experts are now looking for clues about what the bank will do next. Fred Neumann, the chief Asia economist at HSBC, mentioned that the tone of the BoJ’s statement and the fact that two members disagreed with the vote leaves some questions about how aggressive the bank will be in the future. While it seems unlikely that the bank will raise rates in back-to-back meetings, investors will be watching closely to see if officials are prepared to make another move by December.
paragraphs.zh: 專家們現在正尋找關於該行下一步行動的線索。匯豐銀行（HSBC）亞洲首席經濟學家紐曼（Fred Neumann）提到，日本銀行聲明的語氣，以及兩名成員投下反對票的事實，讓人對該行未來採取行動的積極程度產生了一些疑問。雖然該行不太可能在連續的會議中升息，但投資人將密切關注官員們是否準備在十二月採取進一步行動。

paragraphs.en: For now, the Bank of Japan is moving away from its old policy of trying to push inflation up. Instead, it is now focused on making sure inflation does not go too high. If the rate of inflation goes well above 2%, it could hurt the Japanese economy. As the world continues to deal with the fallout from the war in Iran, the BoJ’s next steps will be critical. The bank remains in a phase where it must watch economic data very closely to ensure that Japan’s recovery stays on track without causing new problems for businesses or regular people.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，日本銀行正逐漸脫離過去試圖推升通貨膨脹的舊政策。取而代之的是，該行現在專注於確保通貨膨脹不會過高。如果通貨膨脹率遠高於百分之二，可能會損害日本經濟。隨著世界持續應對伊朗戰爭帶來的後果，日本銀行的下一步行動將至關重要。該行仍處於必須密切觀察經濟數據的階段，以確保日本的復甦保持正軌，同時不會對企業或一般民眾造成新的問題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Making monetary policy more restrictive by raising interest rates to reduce the money supply.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 緊縮（貨幣政策），指透過提高利率來減少市場上的貨幣流通量。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於實體動作（拉緊），這裡指經濟政策的緊縮。文中：central banks in the United States and Europe also tightening monetary policy—a strategy used to control the amount of money in the economy to stop prices from rising too quickly.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A continuous decrease in the value or price of something.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 下滑、跌落，指價值或價格持續下降。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（滑動），這裡作名詞指貨幣價值下跌。文中：helping to stop the currency’s slide to a 40-year low.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To expect that something will fail or decrease in value and act accordingly.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 賭某事物會失敗或價值下跌（看空）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 並非字面上的賭博，而是指金融市場上的看空行為。文中：US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently warned currency traders not to bet against the yen, suggesting that the US and Japan are working together to keep the currency stable.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Happening one after another without a break.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上像背對背，這裡形容會議連續舉行。文中：While it seems unlikely that the bank will raise rates in back-to-back meetings, investors will be watching closely to see if officials are prepared to make another move by December.

quiz.question: What was the specific outcome of the Bank of Japan's policy committee vote regarding the interest rate increase?

options.A: The committee voted unanimously to raise the rate to 1.25%.
options.B: Seven out of nine board members supported the decision to increase the rate.
options.C: The committee was split evenly, with half the members opposing the hike.
options.D: The majority of the committee voted to keep the rate steady at 1%.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，委員會共有九名成員，其中有兩名成員反對此次升息，因此表示有七名成員支持該決策。選項 A 錯誤，因為投票並非一致通過；選項 C 錯誤，因為並非平手；選項 D 錯誤，因為最終結果確實是升息，而非維持原利率。

quiz.question: Based on the article, what can be inferred about the Bank of Japan's future interest rate strategy?

options.A: The bank has committed to raising interest rates every three months.
options.B: The bank will prioritize keeping the yen strong over controlling inflation.
options.C: The bank will remain flexible and data-dependent rather than following a rigid schedule.
options.D: The bank plans to aggressively raise rates until inflation reaches 5%.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，總裁 Kazuo Ueda 明確表示銀行沒有固定的升息時間表（例如每三個月升息一次），而是會根據物價發展與經濟數據來決定。選項 A 與文章內容直接衝突；選項 B 無法從文中推論，因為銀行主要目標是將通膨維持在 2% 左右；選項 D 則完全未在文中提及，且與目標不符。

quiz.question: In the context of the final paragraph, what does the word 'fallout' mean?

options.A: The physical destruction of buildings caused by a conflict.
options.B: The negative side effects or consequences resulting from an event.
options.C: The process of falling down or declining in value.
options.D: The official agreement signed after a war ends.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境中，「fallout」指的是戰爭所引發的後續負面影響或經濟衝擊，而非字面上的放射性塵埃或物理毀壞。選項 A 是過度字面化的解釋；選項 C 雖然描述了價值下降，但在此語境中指的是事件的後果；選項 D 則與「fallout」的定義無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: The Bank of Japan is exclusively focused on strengthening the Japanese yen against the US dollar.
options.B: Global inflation has forced central banks to stop all economic growth initiatives.
options.C: The Bank of Japan is adjusting its monetary policy in response to economic pressures to manage inflation and stabilize the economy.
options.D: The war in Iran is the sole reason for all economic problems currently faced by the Japanese government.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於報導日本央行升息的決策，並解釋此舉是為了應對全球通膨壓力、控制物價並穩定經濟。選項 A 片面，升息雖與匯率有關，但非唯一目標；選項 B 過於誇大，文中並未說停止所有成長計畫；選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到戰爭是經濟壓力的來源之一，而非唯一原因。
